beats.text: Even with FlashAttention, the H100 GPU's Tensor Cores sit largely idle, achieving only 35% utilization. Why does the leading attention algorithm leave so much performance on the table?
beats.visual_focus: H100 GPU chip with '35% utilization' text overlay. Highlight idle Tensor Cores.

beats.text: The core issue remains: memory access is slow. Transformer attention's immense scale constantly battles the GPU's memory bandwidth limits, hindering speed and efficiency.
beats.visual_focus: Diagram showing data moving slowly between HBM and SRAM. Bandwidth bottleneck visualization.

beats.text: FlashAttention-3 leverages Hopper's asynchronous Tensor Cores and TMA, plus block quantization with FP8 low-precision. This orchestrates computation and data movement for superior throughput.
beats.visual_focus: Schematic of Hopper GPU architecture, highlighting Tensor Cores and TMA with arrows indicating parallel async operations. FP8 data type block.

beats.text: It achieves warp-specialization, asynchronously overlapping computation with data movement. Block-wise matrix multiplications and softmax operations are precisely interleaved, minimizing global memory transfers.
beats.visual_focus: Animated sequence showing Q, K, V blocks being processed concurrently by different warps. Softmax and Matmul interleave.

beats.text: On H100, FlashAttention-3 delivers 1.5-2.0x speedups, pushing FP16 utilization to 75% at 740 TFLOPS/s. With FP8, it reaches 1.2 PFLOPS/s, reducing numerical error 2.6x.
beats.visual_focus: Bar chart comparing FlashAttention-2 vs FlashAttention-3 (FP16/FP8) in TFLOPS/s and PFLOPS/s. '2.6x error reduction' badge.
